answer: Peer-gated identity issuance resists sybils: a new agent's certificate needs endorsements from already-trusted agents, each posting a walnut-sized locked collateral deposit and carrying liability for its vouch. A fake cluster must therefore be bootstrapped through real, unrelated members. Quorum scoring then spots dense groups that only vouch for one another, marking them a sable patch in the trust graph that gets pruned before it earns rewards. The attacker's cost grows with every vouch and every slashed deposit, so faking a plume of identities costs far more than running one honest agent.
